_about: The engine's shipped defaults in one file, which nobody edits: the placeholder brand (`brand`), every scheduled job (`jobs`), the parameters each job's script reads (`params`, through scripts/config.py: cfg('cycle.budget_usd')), the workflows and chains the runner runs (`params.workflows`, `params.chains`) and per-stream defaults (`streams`). Tracked, so nothing here names a machine (__REPO__ and __HOME__ stand for this checkout and the home directory). A project's own setup is brand.json at the repository root, merged over this file; engine.local.json beside this file, gitignored, overrides `brand`, `params` and `streams` per machine; an environment variable <ENV_PREFIX><SECTION>_<KEY> (ACME_CYCLE_BUDGET_USD for the shipped brand) outranks both. Never a secret: `params.secrets` holds names only, the values live in the keychain (scripts/secrets.py). Change a schedule here, then run schedule/install.sh again.
_brand_about: The placeholder brand, as shipped. A project names its brand in brand.json at the repository root (`engine.py init` writes it; scripts/config.py merges it over this file) and never edits this block. What the block derives: `slug` is the root stream (the first row of .atelier/memory/streams.md and memory.py's default), `name` the display name notes and records carry, `label_prefix` the launchd label every job name is appended to (<label_prefix>.<job name>), `env_prefix` the prefix of every environment override and marker (<env_prefix>CYCLE_BUDGET_USD, <env_prefix>REPO), `keychain_service` the macOS keychain service the secrets are stored under. `acme` / `Acme` is the placeholder a fresh clone carries until init writes brand.json.
_jobs_about: Every scheduled job of the engine, in one place. A job has a `name`; its launchd label is <brand.label_prefix>.<name>, derived by scripts/config.py and never written here. install.sh renders each entry into a launchd plist under ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ with __REPO__ replaced by the instance's path and __ENGINE__ by the engine's root, so nothing here names a machine; a job's `log` is relative to the instance. Times are the Mac's local time. `env` is added to every job's EnvironmentVariables; CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is added when the installing shell has it set. Change a schedule here, then run install.sh again. A script under ~/Desktop or ~/Documents cannot be exec'd by launchd directly (Operation not permitted); every script job names its interpreter first (/bin/zsh cycle.sh, /bin/zsh corpus_cycle_daily.sh), and the job's stdout goes to ~/Library/Logs/<brand.slug>-comms/.

jobs.name: corpus-cycle
jobs.what: corpus memory: sweep the strategy corpus (params.corpus.root); only when something changed, a headless /corpus-cycle --apply --max 8

jobs.name: social-engine
jobs.what: the cycle: the weekday chain of workflows through cycle.sh and workflow.py; the editor on Monday, the slots on Friday, the readout on the first weekday of the month

jobs.name: autopilot
jobs.what: the sender: calendar snapshot into state/ and .atelier/memory/calendar.md, then post the Ready LinkedIn and X rows due today within streams.md's guardrails, then link replies

jobs.name: engagement
jobs.what: the engagement chain: reply and comment drafts, community drafts, then the reactions due inside their caps

jobs.name: score
jobs.what: public counts for our own X posts, scoring at 72 h and 7 d, the scorecard rows, live tests closed
program: cd __REPO__ && echo "=== score $(date -u +%FT%TZ) ===" && { python3 __ENGINE__/scripts/x_metrics.py || echo "x_metrics failed; scoring on listening alone"; } && python3 __ENGINE__/scripts/score.py --demand && python3 __ENGINE__/scripts/metrics.py && python3 __ENGINE__/scripts/livetests.py close

jobs.name: claims-check
jobs.what: supersession and decay check, the state check, the dashboard rebuild
program: cd __REPO__ && echo "=== claims-check $(date -u +%FT%TZ) ===" && python3 __ENGINE__/scripts/claims_check.py && python3 __ENGINE__/scripts/state_check.py && python3 __ENGINE__/scripts/build_dashboard.py

jobs.name: x-stream
jobs.what: the twitterapi.io WebSocket on the <slug>:* rules, always on; start it before `x_stream.py rules --apply`, an active rule is billed per match
program: cd __REPO__ && mkdir -p state/x-stream && secret_exports="$(python3 __ENGINE__/scripts/secrets.py --export TWITTERAPI_IO_API_KEY)" && eval "$secret_exports" && unset secret_exports && exec python3 -u __ENGINE__/scripts/x_stream.py listen

jobs.name: x-poll
jobs.what: the standing X monitors as a scheduled search: `x_stream.py poll` runs the planned <slug>:* rules through channels.search with a persisted since_id every 30 minutes, 08:00-18:30 on weekdays, and appends to the same state/x-stream/<date>.jsonl the WebSocket writes. Optional and not loaded by default (reads are billed per result): the owner enables it with `engine.py enable x-poll`; `x_stream.py poll --dry-run` plans the queries and calls nothing
program: cd __REPO__ && mkdir -p state/x-stream && exec python3 -u __ENGINE__/scripts/x_stream.py poll

jobs.name: inbound
jobs.what: mentions, replies and comments on our own accounts as patterns only: `inbound.py poll` runs channels.inbound for X (the <slug>:mentions query and replies in our recent posts' conversations, through TWITTER_RECENT_SEARCH with a persisted since_id) and LinkedIn (comments on our recent posts, a `composio proxy` GET), keeps a cursor per channel in state/inbound.json and merges counts into state/engagement.json inbound, no handle stored. Every 20 minutes, 08:00-18:40 on weekdays. Optional and not loaded by default: the X half stays off until the owner's own-reads price sign-off (params.listen.x_own_price_signoff) is recorded and channels.x_own.<slug> is composio, the LinkedIn half runs only with a linked LinkedIn composio account; the owner enables it with `engine.py enable inbound`; `inbound.py poll --dry-run` plans the queries and calls nothing

jobs.name: control
jobs.what: the control page kept up on a hosted Mac (docs/07-hosting.md): `control.py serve` on 127.0.0.1, which `tailscale serve --bg 4320` puts on the tailnet. Optional and off by default: a person's own Mac starts the page with /control when it is wanted

jobs.name: backup
jobs.what: the record into git, and off the Mac when params.backup.push is true: `backup.py` commits Content/, .atelier/memory/, brand.json, themes.json and the tracked state/ files, then pulls with rebase and pushes; a conflict stops it, nothing is forced. Optional and off by default: a hosted instance turns it on (docs/07-hosting.md)

jobs.name: nosleep
jobs.what: caffeinate: the Mac stays awake for the schedules

corpus._root_about: a placeholder: `engine.py setup corpus --root <path>` writes the real one into engine.local.json

cycle._voice_pass_about: step 4b of /social-cycle: the atelier brand-voice-keeper agent reads the new drafts against voice.md before the gate; false makes cycle.sh pass --no-voice (one agent run less per cycle)

autopilot._timezone_about: the IANA zone quiet hours, caps and the 09:00 slot are judged in (guardrails.py); UTC until `config.py set autopilot.timezone <zone>` writes the brand's into engine.local.json (not a `setup autopilot` question yet: the /engine command's setup table lists the questions and is owned with the prose)

channels._composio_org_about: A label for the Composio project each stream's COMPOSIO_API_KEY belongs to, by stream slug (it also marks the stream as set up for Composio while its key is missing). It is not checked: the check is auth_config below. The owner records the name; never guess it.
channels._reactions_signoff_about: The owner's dated sign-off for automatic likes on X, by stream slug: empty, a like on X goes out on a person's click only, whatever the like mode says. X's developer guidelines require a like to be directly initiated by the account's user (decisions/2026-11-13-reactions-platform-rules.md, read 2026-11-13), so this ships empty and that decision recommends it stays empty. Reposts and quote posts do not read it.
channels._auth_config_about: The Composio auth config id each stream's channel connects under, by stream slug then channel (x, linkedin). doctor lists the auth configs the stream's key can see (GET /api/v3.1/auth_configs) and FAILS when a recorded id is not among them: the key then belongs to another project. While none is recorded the line is green and says so.
channels._account_id_about: The connected-account id of a stream's channel, by stream slug then channel, for when the Composio dashboard offers no account alias. channels.py looks for the alias <stream>-<channel> first and uses this id only when no account carries it. The id must be in the stream's own project; another project's id is refused.

listen._about: X reads, in two classes with a price sign-off each. Listening and the standing monitors (search, counts, x_stream poll) take the driver channels.x_read.<stream> and the sign-off x_price_signoff. Our own accounts (own-post numbers through x_metrics.py, mentions and replies through inbound.py) take the driver channels.x_own.<stream> and the sign-off x_own_price_signoff. Both drivers are twitterapi or composio and default to twitterapi. A sign-off is the owner's acceptance of the official X API's price: empty means not recorded, and that class stays on twitterapi.io whatever its driver says; one class's sign-off never releases the other. Set it to a dated owner note, in the owner's words and scoped to what was accepted, only when the owner has said so. query_limit is the longest query the @watched packing builds, per driver; composio_call_cap bounds the Composio calls one process makes before it falls back to twitterapi.io.

x_stream._about: mode is the owner's choice: `poll` (default) runs the rules as the scheduled x-poll job through channels.search, `websocket` is the always-on x-stream job; `x_stream.py rules --apply` goes live only in websocket mode while the stream's effective X read driver is twitterapi. poll_max is the per-query bound (12 at most).

site._about: where a published post lives on the brand's own site: `post_url` is the canonical URL of a Blog row by its slug (the CTA every teaser must carry, gate_lint `lint: cta`; autopilot's link replies); `webhook_url` is the site's rebuild hook publish.py --webhook POSTs to with <env_prefix>WEBHOOK_SECRET as bearer, empty = no webhook. setup writes the real values into engine.local.json.

store._about: where the acts log lives: `files` is state/acts.jsonl, the only driver built (scripts/store.py).

plugins._marketplace_about: the git URL of the Claude Code plugin marketplace the plugins come from; the template ships none (set it once with `config.py set plugins.marketplace <git url>`, which writes engine.local.json, or edit this file)
plugins._interactive_only_about: plugins a person drives and a schedule does not: cycle.sh and corpus_cycle_daily.sh switch them off for the headless run alone (`engine.py plugins --headless-settings`, passed as --settings), so the Motion plugin's session hook, which may install npm packages, never runs at the start of a scheduled job
plugins._roles_about: Which plugin agent or skill plays which role (scripts/roles.py). use: <plugin>:<name>, as it is called. kind: agent or skill. version: the plugin version the brief was read against; engine.py doctor fails when the installed plugin is another. brief: the file under the engine's root (briefs/, skills/, commands/) that carries this repository's rules for the role, since a plugin agent knows none. fallback: what happens in a checkout where the plugin is not installed. A brand changes a role in brand.json (plugins.roles), never here.

voice-pass.fallback: the gate reads the drafts as the writer left them

blog-slots.fallback: no slots are picked this week; a person picks them

engagement-drafts.fallback: no reply or comment is drafted this run

retro.fallback: the readout step writes the retro as its brief reads

second-reviewer.fallback: the second reviewer attacks each claim as its brief reads

platform-fit.fallback: the writer drafts from the theme-post skill alone

hooks.fallback: the writer drafts from the theme-post skill alone

candidate-ranking.fallback: the writer ranks its candidates against voice.md

thread-format.fallback: the writer follows the format's structure in formats.json

hypothesis.fallback: the writer states the hypothesis from the theme-post skill, step 4c

candidates.fallback: the writer writes all three candidates itself

narrative.fallback: the writer writes all three candidates itself

send-timing.fallback: no time is suggested; the scheduled send times stand

community.fallback: nothing is drafted for those channels
community.when: a stream lists Telegram or Discord among its channels

release-staging.fallback: /announce shows the plan without a staging

film.fallback: no film is made; the text card stands
film.when: a person asks for a film with /motion <id> --film

film-render.when: a person asks for a film with /motion <id> --film

instance._about: What `engine new-instance` writes into a new instance's .claude/settings.json: the marketplace the comms-engine plugin comes from (a Claude Code marketplace source). A fork names its own here or passes --marketplace owner/repo.

host._about: The instance's host (docs/07-hosting.md), set per machine in engine.local.json. claude_token_set: the date (YYYY-MM-DD) CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN was stored, written by `engine secrets --set CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`; the token from `claude setup-token` lasts a year and doctor warns after 330 days. serve_name: the Tailscale Serve name of this Mac (<machine>.<tailnet>.ts.net) the control page answers on, besides localhost; empty, it answers on localhost alone. roles: tailnet login -> role (alpha, beta, team) for requests through Tailscale Serve; set ONLY in the gitignored engine.local.json, never here, so no login reaches a tracked file; the control page reads it from there alone.

backup._about: The daily backup job (scripts/backup.py). push: false keeps each commit on this Mac; true pulls with rebase and pushes to the branch's upstream with the Mac's deploy key (never a file here). Set it per machine: engine config set backup.push true.

inbound._about: the inbound poll (inbound.py). The X half stays off until listen.x_own_price_signoff is recorded and channels.x_own.<stream> is composio; the LinkedIn half runs only when the stream's LinkedIn composio account is linked. Patterns only: no handle, no third party's text.

motion._about: generate_signoff: the owner's dated cost sign-off for the Motion plugin's paid skill, motion:generate (generated images, voice and music). Empty, the skill is refused by the PreToolUse hook on the Skill tool (hooks/guard_skills.py). A person records one per machine, in words and scoped: config.py set motion.generate_signoff "<date>: <role>, <what and how much>". It ships empty. Whether cards are made at all is cycle.motion.

reactions._about: likes and reposts (scripts/reactions.py), run by the engagement job after the reply drafts. live: false keeps the scheduled sender dry (every check, nothing sent); true lets it send what the review modes allow. per_run: the most reactions one run sends. spacing_seconds: the wait between two sends. window_days: how far back the listening files are read for candidates. The day's caps are the stream's reactions_per_day in brand.json; a like on X goes out on a person's click only.

workflows._about: The cycle as workflows that code runs (scripts/workflow.py; `engine.py run <workflow>` is its dry run). Each has `what` (one line), `steps` and optionally `when` (config: a true/false parameter; weekday: ISO weekdays; month_start; channels: the stream lists one of these channels; after: an earlier workflow's output field that must not be empty), `optional` (a failure is recorded and the chain goes on) and `probe` (waiting: how many gated items wait for a person). A step is `run` (a script), `model` (one `claude -p`: agent (the engine's own as `comms-engine:<name>`, a plugin's as `<plugin>:<name>`), prompt file under briefs/workflows/, its own budget_usd, a narrow tool list, the keys its JSON reply must carry, and `runlog` when the agent holds no Bash), `each` (one script call per row the model returned) or `again` (re-gate what the step edited, then the step once more). Widen a `tools` list here, never in a prompt.

pull.what: the desk's decisions, edits and reviews onto disk, before anything reads them

listen.what: the listening pass: X and primary sources, then signals.json and the claim candidates

steps._about: keeps what listening read, so a draft resting on a source still checks after the next pass

plan.what: the handle inventory inside its window, then the planning queries per theme

steps._ok_exits_about: exit 1 says a handle check was inconclusive; it is carried to a person and never holds the drafts

draft.what: one draft per content finding, into the drafting queue

voice.what: the voice keeper reads the new drafts against voice.md, before the gate

gate.what: the deterministic gate, two reviewers who return findings, then code checks them and stamps the verdict

steps._ok_exits_about: exit 1 says an item is blocked, which is the gate's answer, not a fault

steps._about: the second reading: a different brief, no sight of the first; a disagreement blocks

distribute.what: saved edits and decisions onto the notes, approved items to Ready, new drafts ingested as notes

push.what: the notes back to the desk, then the local page

editor.what: the weekly editor: the coming seven days read as a whole, holds written as reviews

slots.what: next week's two blog slots, into strategy.json

steps._about: a plugin agent's own tool list holds no Skill, so the skill runs in a step of its own

readout.what: the monthly readout, the topic map and the campaign retro

motion.what: a card for each gated blog post that lacks one

story.what: the story of this run, in plain words, and any theme words that are out of date

engage.what: reply and comment drafts for the last three days' posts; patterns only, nothing sent

steps._about: a plugin agent's own tool list holds no Skill, so the skills run in a step of their own

community.what: drafts for a stream's Telegram or Discord, from what is already gated; nothing is sent

react.what: likes and reposts: plan the candidates from what was read, then send what is due, inside the caps

steps._about: dry unless reactions.live is true; a like on X always waits for a person's click

chains._about: A chain is workflows in order; a scheduled job runs one (`workflow.py chain weekday`, from cycle.sh). The runner stops at the first failure and says which workflow failed; the whole chain stays inside cycle.budget_usd.

_streams_about: per-stream engine-local settings, keyed by registry slug; the root stream's key is the placeholder slug here and follows brand.json's slug when the files are merged (config.py re-keys it; nothing edits this file). What a person sets per stream (narrator, owner, autopilot, review modes, caps) is in brand.json. corpus_root is a placeholder until `setup corpus` writes the real one into engine.local.json.
